3GPP TSG RAN meeting #83 was held in Shenzhen, China, March 18-21, 2019, hosted by Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. The meeting had 280 participants (see Annex A) and 773 Technical Documents (see Annex B). Main topics/decisions: - block approval: RAN #83 continued to use "block approval process" for agreed CR packages from WGs and WI/SI status reports, i.e. these contributions were only discussed on request (flag) otherwise the CRs were considered approved and the status reports are noted. - time budget analysis: RAN #83 assessed the modified time budget requests in WI/SI status reports for already approved WIs/SIs relative to the time budget status endorsed by RAN #82 in RP-182904; the RAN WG chairmen provided their estimates of remaining time budgets in their WGs (see e.g. WG status reports); new WIs/SIs provided their time budget requests in the WI/SI descriptions; the resulting time budget allocations for all approved WIs/SIs after RAN #83 were endorsed by email in RP-190641 (1 time unit (TU) ~ 2h). RAN5 WIs/SIs are excluded from this time budget handling. - REL-14 (was frozen in March 17, ASN.1 was frozen in June 17): Status after RAN #82: No open REL-14 Core and no open REL-14 Perf. part WIs. But after RAN #83, there are still 3 open REL-13 and 5 open REL-14 testing WIs ongoing. - ... - A joint RAN-SA session was held on Wed evening of TSG #83 treating 3 Tdocs (RP-190716, RP-190718, RP-190736): endorsed to have a 15 months/5 quarter REL-17 (in Sep.19 we will check whether this is possible; by Dec.19 the REL-17 schedule will be fixed). - Liaison statements/Letters to ITU: incoming: 62, outgoing 10 (see Annex C) - WI summary: At RAN #83, a WI summary (descriptive summary of the features actually included in the specs) was presented for the following 1 WI: - REL-16 WI Iuant_transfer-Core RP-190144 Note: The rapporteur has to provide a WI summary to the RAN meeting at which a Core part WI is declared to be 100% complete; this WI summary has to be reviewed by the leading WG of the WI beforehand to check the technical correctness.

As RAN5 prepares for 6G, the group faces a structural challenge: we must develop 6G conformance test specifications while continuing to maintain the accumulated 5G-Advanced test specifications. The workload is already at a scale that strains the current way of working, and the addition of 6G will increase it further. Analysis of RAN5 meeting TDocList from RAN5#76 (Berlin, 2017) to RAN5#111 (Dalian, 2026) shows that the 5GS_NR_LTE-UEConTest [1] work item alone has produced: - 19,640 TDocs across 36 meetings, of which 17,083 are CRs (87%) - 9,495 CRs agreed (56% of all CRs) - 1,307 discussion papers - Generating 15 new TS/TR and impacted 14 existing TS/TR for RAN5. RAN5 has sustained 1,000-2,000+ TDocs per meeting for nearly a decade. From R16 to R19, 173 5G related UE conformance test work items have been created (31 in R16, 53 in R17, 55 in R18, 34 in R19). A significant portion of these work items is pattern-driven: CADC configurations, HPUE power classes and new bands/BW additions follow well-established templates once the first example test case exists. This repetitive work consumes substantial meeting time and expert effort. The 6G specification modernization study (6GSM, [2][3]) addresses format and tooling aspects such as Markdown and GIT/forge. The RAN5 group has already begun discussing 6G testing and conformance requirements from multiple angles, including test efficiency and simplification [4], WI admission mechanisms [5][6], SIG/RRM overlap reduction [7], 6G RRM requirements [8], PRD21 continuation [9] and SIG readiness [10]. However, AI-assisted workflow efficiency has not yet been formally discussed in RAN5. We believe it should be a complementary track, started now in 5G-Advanced and matured before 6G test specification work begins. Athens, Greece 25 Feb – 1 Mar 2019 Purpose: For information In order to assist RAN5 delegates to plan their submissions over the next 3 months, the deadlines that cover the period 4 Mar 2019 – 13 May 2019 are provided below: * It should be noted that company contributions (i.e. those not formally agreed at the WG) may be submitted directly to the RAN Plenary (independently of RAN5). I will present contributions on behalf of a company at the Plenary (wearing my Chair hat) if requested. The benefit of uploading documents on time is to ensure that interested parties have a reasonable time (a minimum of 5 working days for a regular meeting) to review the documents prior to the start of the RAN5 meeting. This is especially important for CRs that require a verdict at the meeting. Late docs may still be uploaded to the reflector but whilst tolerance is often shown by delegates, such documents may be deferred if more time is requested. Delegates requiring Tdoc numbers after the 3GU has closed should apply to the Convenor prior to the start of the meeting no later than the COB on the Monday after 3GU closure. The strong advice is to use the 3GU when available. For details on the process for revising CRs and the allocation of new Tdoc numbers after the meeting has started please refer to RAN5 PRD15: Document Issuance at WG Level. It should also be noted that delegates must take care to select the correct agenda item, Work Item Code, TS version number when using the 3GU. Failure to do so creates nugatory work for the Secretary and wastes meeting time. It may also mean that documents could be presented for approval at the Plenary incorrectly with the possibility that such documents are rejected. Athens, Greece 25 Feb – 1 Mar 2019 Purpose: For information In order to assist RAN5 delegates to plan their submissions over the next 3 months, the deadlines that cover the period 4 Mar 2019 – 13 May 2019 are provided below: * It should be noted that company contributions (i.e. those not formally agreed at the WG) may be submitted directly to the RAN Plenary (independently of RAN5). I will present contributions on behalf of a company at the Plenary (wearing my Chair hat) if requested. The benefit of uploading documents on time is to ensure that interested parties have a reasonable time (a minimum of 5 working days for a regular meeting) to review the documents prior to the start of the RAN5 meeting. This is especially important for CRs that require a verdict at the meeting. Late docs may still be uploaded to the reflector but whilst tolerance is often shown by delegates, such documents may be deferred if more time is requested. Delegates requiring Tdoc numbers after the 3GU has closed should apply to the Convenor prior to the start of the meeting no later than the COB on the Monday after 3GU closure. The strong advice is to use the 3GU when available. For details on the process for revising CRs and the allocation of new Tdoc numbers after the meeting has started please refer to RAN5 PRD15: Document Issuance at WG Level. It should also be noted that delegates must take care to select the correct agenda item, Work Item Code, TS version number when using the 3GU. Failure to do so creates nugatory work for the Secretary and wastes meeting time. It may also mean that documents could be presented for approval at the Plenary incorrectly with the possibility that such documents are rejected.
